image_description: A group of four people posing for a portrait, likely at a graduation ceremony. The subjects are wearing black academic gowns and mortarboard caps. The person in the foreground right is smiling and holding a diploma scroll. The person in the foreground left holds a white cane or rod. Two figures stand in the background, one raising a fist. The lighting is warm and studio-like with a blurred golden/brown background.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The garments are cropped at the waist or thighs due to the image framing; the 'ankles' part of the checkpoint cannot be verified, and the visible portion shows significant bunching rather than a clean rectangular drape.

While generally symmetrical, the front openings are obscured by folds, arms, and held objects (diploma, cane). The closure panels do not hang cleanly as described; they appear merged or irregularly folded.
The gowns are loose and hide the underlying body shape effectively.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The sleeves on the main subject (right) show purple bars but do not exhibit the characteristic 'bell' shape hanging below the hand; they appear more like standard jacket sleeves or are tucked/obscured. The distinctive wide academic sleeve drape is missing or poorly rendered.
Distinct, separate front panels are not clearly visible; the fabric appears to merge or fold unnaturally near the chest.
Collars of shirts and ties are visible underneath the gowns.

No strong specular highlights are present on the gown surfaces.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: As noted in functional components, the specific academic sleeve drape is absent. The sleeves terminate near the wrist or are indistinguishable from the arm position.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The fingers of the subject on the right merge into the diploma scroll without clear digit separation. The hands of the subject on the left gripping the white cane appear melted and structurally ambiguous, lacking distinct knuckles and fingernails.

The faces of the two background figures are distorted and lack coherent facial features. The mortarboard cap on the back-left figure seems to float or attach at an impossible angle relative to the head.
Some folds in the black fabric appear smudged or painterly rather than crisp textile folds. Edges where the gown meets the background show slight haloing/bleeding.
The cylinder shape of the diploma is inconsistent, appearing to flatten and widen unnaturally in the middle, defying rigid object geometry.
